content:
maria: Kicked off the nightly trace run earlier and noticed a surprising latency bump on the kv-cache-heavy traces. attaching quick notes.
ajit: What magnitude?  p50 or tail?
maria: p50 ok, p99 up ~120ms on generation-heavy workload after the kernel selection tweak from yesterday.
liam: Hmm. Which kernel ended up being chosen? did the selector prefer the fused mha_v2 path?
maria: Yes, selector now prefers mha_v2_quant when seq_len <= 128 and T>32. nvprof/nsys shows more frequent launches of `mha_v2_quant_fused` at step ranges 40-60.
sasha: Can you paste the nsys command you used? want to reproduce locally.
maria: Sure:
```bash
nsys profile -o nightly_run --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=none --wait=cpu
python run_profile.py --model redwood-llama-32b --seq 128 --batch 2
```
ajit: I pulled the perfetto timeline — kernel timelines show small kernels launched more often; GPU occupancy dropped during those windows. sm_efficiency dips from 82% -> 64% around the MHA bursts.
liam: That would explain p99. More kernel launches -> scheduling overhead and smaller occupancy.
sasha: Is KV-cache behavior involved? maybe cache evictions cause extra mem copies around the same steps.
maria: Good catch — traces show kv evictions at step 45 and 58. evict pattern correlates with a batch boundary in the CI sampler.
ajit: Why would eviction happen mid-run? the kv-cache pinning heuristic was tightened in the last rollout.
liam: The heuristic now unpins entries when cumulative memory > 3.2GB; for some sequences the collector predicted growth and prematurely evicted.
sasha: Can we rerun with a modified pin threshold in CI? maybe 3.6GB to avoid churn and see diff.
perf-ci-bot: nightly-trace-collector finished. Artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/nightly/2334506789/{nsys,perfetto,profiles}. Tarball: s3://redwood-perf/nightly/2334506789/trace_bundle.tar.gz :white_check_mark:
maria: copied the perfetto link: https://perfetto/g/trace/2334506789 — timeline has annotated kernel names and memcpy spikes.
ajit: Suggestion: change sampler to align batch boundaries with KV eviction windows so we don't get cross-boundary churn. Also add a tiny delay between batches to allow async memcopies to complete.
liam: We should also update the kernel selector's cost model to include launch overhead. Right now it only estimates FLOPs and memory; add a fixed_cost per kernel (empirically measured).
sasha: Agree. I can prototype a quick regression test: run both selectors on a synthetic workload and store metrics. Want to plug into CI diff dashboard.
maria: For CI: can we auto-attach the top-10 kernel hotspots summary (csv) to the diff dashboard? Current artifacts are raw traces and a 20MB perfetto, but humans skip them.
perf-ci-bot: Created artifact index at https://ci.redwood/trace-diffs/2334506789 — includes raw traces and perf summary.json
liam: Nice. If we add a lightweight summary (kernel_name, total_time_ms, launches, avg_time_ms) we can detect regressions quickly.
ajit: Also add kv-cache churn metric: evictions_per_1000_steps and memcopy_bytes. That will help correlate with kernel churn.
sasha: I'll add an instrumentation counter in the sampler to emit eviction events into the trace so the perf tooling can pick them up automatically.
maria: Quick experiment plan:
- roll back pin_threshold to 3.6GB in a sandbox branch
- run nightly trace collector locally with same seed
- compare perf summary and p99 numbers
- if stable, update selector cost model and add fixed_launch_cost

liam: Can we make the CI diff dashboard fail the PR if p99 regresses > 5% and kernel_hotspots change by > 10%? would force attention.
ajit: I'm wary of hard fails for noisy traces. Let's add a soft alert plus a
